package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'boto3' AWS SDK, containing heavily obfuscated and encrypted malicious code that establishes a remote command-and-control channel, exfiltrates sensitive host data, and enables arbitrary remote code execution. It masquerades as a legitimate package by bundling the real 'boto3' but executes a sophisticated backdoor at install time.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import base64, itertools
exec(''.join(chr(c^k) for c,k in zip(base64.b64decode('b'...'), itertools.cycle(b'869bd633fef02645b114af5158834a2f'))).encode())
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code decodes a base64-encoded, XOR-encrypted payload and executes it, launching the main malicious agent.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code using both base64 and XOR encryption is a strong indicator of malicious intent, especially when executed automatically during installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only contain installation logic, not arbitrary code execution or obfuscated payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used in proprietary software to protect intellectual property, but never in open-source install scripts.
key_indicators: Use of exec on decoded/encrypted data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install and runtime, the code establishes a persistent connection to a remote C2 server, checks in with host details, and enters a loop to receive and execute attacker-supplied commands.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing a remote connection to an untrusted server and entering a persistent command loop is classic C2/backdoor behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not connect to external servers or await remote commands post-install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management agents (with user consent) may use similar patterns, but never in a library or SDK.

    'os': self.getOSVersion(),
    'user': self.getUsername(),
    'host': socket.gethostname(),
    'fqdn': socket.getfqdn(),
    'pid': os.getpid(),
    'uuid': self.agent_config['PayloadUUID'],

  ...

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install/runtime, the code collects host identifiers (IP, OS, username, hostname, FQDN, PID, UUID, encryption keys) and exfiltrates them to the attacker's server via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating detailed host and user information to an external server is a clear sign of reconnaissance and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect or transmit such sensitive information without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise inventory agents may collect similar data, but only with user/admin approval.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code retrieves attacker-supplied commands from the C2 server and executes them in new threads, enabling arbitrary code execution, file operations, environment variable access, and reverse shells.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Receiving and executing arbitrary remote commands is the hallmark of a backdoor/RAT.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate SDK or library should execute remote code or commands from an untrusted source.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools (with explicit consent) may use similar logic.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated payload is executed during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Decrypted malicious agent is loaded and run.

attack_chain.action: Malicious agent establishes connection to attacker's C2 server and checks in with host details.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim host is registered with C2 and awaits further instructions.

attack_chain.action: Agent enters persistent loop, requesting and executing attacker-supplied commands (arbitrary code, file operations, reverse shells, etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains full remote control and data exfiltration capability.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or encrypted payloads in setup.py or install scripts
Automatic network connections to untrusted domains during or after installation
Exfiltration of host/user/environment data to external servers
Persistent background loops awaiting remote commands
Execution of arbitrary code or shell commands from remote sources
file_indicators: setup.py containing base64 and XOR obfuscation
Presence of a 'KillDate' or similar time-based logic in install scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for obfuscated or encrypted code in setup.py or other install-time scripts, especially those using exec on decoded data. Flag any package that initiates outbound network connections to untrusted domains during installation or runtime. Detect exfiltration of host/user/environment data to known malicious domains. Look for persistent background processes or threads that fetch and execute remote commands. Use file and network IOCs to block or quarantine suspicious packages.
